blocks.text: The place we hoped might help us breathe again
blocks.rawHtml: The place we hoped might help us breathe again

blocks.text: In some ways, this story began in July of 2022.
blocks.rawHtml: In some ways, this story began in July of 2022.

blocks.text: In other ways, it started earlier than that, after cancer had already changed the shape of our lives.
blocks.rawHtml: In other ways, it started earlier than that, after cancer had already changed the shape of our lives.

blocks.text: Vanessa had made it through breast cancer after rounds of chemotherapy and radiation. By the time we bought the property, she was done with treatment, but that does not mean life had simply snapped back to normal. We were both still shaken. Still stressed. Still carrying around the heaviness that comes after something like that. Cancer is not subtle. It is not poetic. It is hard, direct, exhausting, and life-changing. And after all of it, we knew we needed something quieter and more peaceful.

blocks.text: There was junk everywhere. Old broke-down cars. Trailers. An RV or something sitting there. The whole place looked like it had been abandoned in stages. As we walked the property, we kept finding half-finished projects and rough little setups that looked like somebody had started building a dream and then stopped somewhere in the middle.

We searched around, made calls, worked with the credit union that was handling the loan, and kept pushing forward until we finally found a company willing to insure the property.

blocks.text: Technically, the previous owner was still allowed on the property for another couple of days to finish up, but by the following morning he was gone. Before he left, he spent a little time with us, talking, showing us around, and helping us understand the place a little better. Then he was off, and for the next couple of days before we had to return to the city, the property was finally ours.

blocks.text: There was already more to work with than you might have guessed at first glance. The property already had about a dozen young fruit trees, around a year old at the time, including cherry, apple, pear, and peach. It gave us a glimpse of what this place might one day provide.
